audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 2, 3 and first item are given to Quinn while their whys[] describe Maokai landing an undodgeable root and out-sustaining her; Levels 4-5 and 6 are marked Skill while their whys say the trade repeats in Maokai's favour and that R shuts off her only defence. The lane is also labelled TRICKY 7.5/10 against a 60.38% win rate.
audit.why: Twisted Advance is a targeted dash — Quinn's entire kit is mobility and range, and none of it dodges a lock-on root. Once W is up she cannot refuse a trade, and Sap Magic refunds the Vault poke. She only escapes Maokai by leaving the lane, which is why 2+ items flattens rather than favours either side.
audit.corrected: Rows 1-5 set to Maokai in both layers, row 6 left as the packet's Skill, difficulty relabelled EVEN at 5/10.

audit.why: Four spikes present: Lvl 2-3 targeted root, Lvl 6 escape denial, 1st item stability, Late as her map phase. The last one is the right read — her threat window is the map, not the duel.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[0] is titled 'Fight into her blind' and never says what the blind does or does not stop. dontsFull[1] is titled 'Poke-war from range' with no ranges given. Vault has no cooldown anywhere.
audit.why: Blinding Assault causes miss on basic attacks only — it stops Maokai's autos and therefore his Sap Magic proc, but it does nothing to Bramble Smash, Twisted Advance or Nature's Grasp. A player who reads 'don't fight into her blind' will hold the whole combo when only the auto is affected. On ranges, Blinding Assault reaches 1025 against Bramble Smash's 600, so a poke war is unwinnable and walking her down is the answer. Vault is 12/11/10/9/8s.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[0].d now states what the blind does and does not stop; dontsFull[1].d gives both ranges; dosFull[0].d gives Vault's 12s and restates that W is targeted.
sources: champ-data/_kits/quinn.json (Q range and cooldown, E cooldown)

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart and difficulty label taught the opposite of the file's own late[]: 'You win the straight 1v1 all game — she can't kite a targeted root.'
audit.why: Labelling a 60% matchup TRICKY at 7.5/10 makes a Maokai player play scared in a lane he should be forcing, and the common mistake here is exactly that — farming out a lane where he should be walking her down before she can leave for a roam.
audit.corrected: diff, tone, diffRating, breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t all moved to EVEN / 5/10.

edits.before: Passive heal + AA trades carry the early waves. Identify how Quinn contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: One ability and no combo against her Vault poke — neither of you has a kill setup yet, so farm and set up Level 2.

edits.before: W root is your engage AND your peel — spend it once per fight. Only take the trade when Quinn's Vault is down.
edits.after: W is point-and-click, so her Harrier kite and Vault cannot dodge the root that sets up your whole trade.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Quinn must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: W-Q-E lets you root, knock her into your wave, and heal the Vault poke back — she cannot out-DPS your Sap Magic.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Vault's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Your W root repeats on a 12s cooldown and Sap Magic refunds every trade — her poke never out-paces the heal through 4-5.

edits.before: Nature’s Grasp roots whole teams — lane it only for kill windows. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Quinn's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Nature's Grasp walls off her escape lane, so you root her at range and then walk in with W-Q — mobility was her only defence.

edits.before: Heartsteel is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Vault's cooldown.
edits.after: The Bami line plus your repeating W root makes you lane-stable while her poke stalls out.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Quinn carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: She stops dueling and turns into roams and splitpush — follow the wave and ping her missing, since you cannot chase.

edits.before: Her self-peel. Root around it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Her self-peel, 12s at rank 1. W is targeted — it cannot dodge it.

edits.before: That is Quinn's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Blinding Assault blocks your autos and Sap Magic proc, but never your Q or W.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Her Q reaches 1025 and your Q only 600 — walk her down instead.

notes: Best correction here is the blind: 'don't fight into her blind' with no explanation teaches a player to hold their entire combo, when Blinding Assault only affects basic attacks — Bramble Smash, Twisted Advance and Nature's Grasp all land through it. The Sap Magic proc is the one thing it does cost you. Chart rows 1-6 flipped in matched pairs, and a 60.38% lane no longer reads TRICKY 7.5/10. NOTE: whys[0] and early[] both say 'Level 1 is hers', but the packet chart and both layers say Skill for row 0 — I left the enum alone and rewrote the why to be genuinely neutral rather than pick a side against the packet.
